pr_title: net: if: Add IPv4 support to multicast monitor
pr_body:
Make multicast group join/leave monitor support both IPv6 and IPv4 addresses.

Fixes #26585

Signed-off-by: Markus Fuchs <markus.fuchs@ch.sauter-bc.com>
pr_comments:
> The `drivers/can/can_net.c` is also using the multicast monitor API, you need to change that too.

I somehow missed that. Thanks for the hint.

> seems not enable ipv4 multicast in driver level, do we plan to do it in another PR?

Yes, that should be done in other PRs. I'll take care of the STM32 Ethernet driver as that's the hardware I have at hand.

> This is an API change (although very minor and probably does not affect any component outside current drivers), so we should document this in release note.

@jukkar, added a short description to the release notes.

issue_context.title: IPv4 multicast datagrams can't be received for mimxrt1064_evk board (missing ethernet API)
comments: For IPv6 there is `net_if_mcast_mon_register()` that can be used to register a function that will be called if a multicast address is added/removed to the network interface. That function should have IPv4 address support and then we could enhance the IPv4 support in the driver side. I am not convinced that we should have this implemented via `set_config()`.

@jukkar i've looked at the driver and adding the driver part is not difficult we have to re-purpose `net_if_mcast_cb` and remove ipv6 configuration, also re-purposing `net_if_mcast_mon_register()` is not difficult.
However I need to ask you don't we need to add some new ipv4 functions/events/handles that handle joining/leaving ethernet multicast groups? I.e. networking stack support.

> However I need to ask you don't we need to add some new ipv4 functions/events/handles that handle joining/leaving ethernet multicast groups? I.e. networking stack support.

Yes, we need to join/leave multicast group when IPv4 address is added/removed to/from network interface. Sorry for not being more clear in my words above. So this would need to be implemented, basically the functionality should be similar as with IPv6.

On the issue of adding join/leave API, is this something that is generically needed across all drivers?

Also, if we add the .set_config would that be enough to close this ticket?

> On the issue of adding join/leave API, is this something that is generically needed across all drivers?

Probably yes, typically (at least for IPv6 mcast msg) the driver needs to program the Ethernet controller so that it can receive the multicast packets.

> Also, if we add the .set_config would that be enough to close this ticket?

We have an API where a driver can register a function to be called when net stack joins/leaves a multicast group. Right now that API supports only IPv6 addresses. That API would need to be extended to support also IPv4 addresses. See for example `drivers/ethernet/eth_mcux.c`and search for `net_if_mcast_mon_register()` to see how it is used.

But this is only part of the story as also network stack would need to support IPv4 multicast handling similar way as what have been done for IPv6. Right now there is an API to add a IPv4 multicast address to the network interface `net_if_ipv4_maddr_add(()` but it does not trigger a call to multicast monitoring which would inform the driver that the multicast group needs to be joined.
Changes to the code to support this are not very big, it is just that someone needs to join the dots to make this work and test it properly.
@jukkar, If I'm understanding you then it seems like this isn't a platform specific bug?
@dleach02 First of all, this is not a bug, we are just missing a feature. And second, this is not a platform specific issue.
Cool... so @jukkar we can convert this to an enhancement request then?

> we can convert this to an enhancement request then?

Yep, done.

review_comments: I'd be good to move the Ethernet driver changes to a separate commit, they don't seem to be cover in the commit message (and are not related to the core IP stack changes).
As for the drivers that are currently making use of the mcast monitor, I just tried to make sure that their functionality is preserved.
Why this change? I think we should start to monitor multicast addresses only when the user wants to join the multicast group, and not when a multicast address is added to the network interface.

I wanted the `net_if_ipv*_maddr_add()` and `net_if_ipv*_maddr_rm()` functions to behave the same way for IPv4 and IPv6 as the mcast monitor is going to be used by Ethernet drivers to adjust their multicast address filters.
However, you are right, the existing behavior should be maintained (not only because it's the _multicast group join/leave monitor_). I reverted this change.
Note that we currently support also IPv4 IGMP (so similar API as for IPv6 MLD). There exists `net_ipv4_igmp_join()` and `net_ipv4_igmp_leave()` functions and you should tweak those for IPv4 support.

These functions make use of `net_if_ipv4_maddr_add()` and `net_if_ipv4_maddr_rm()` which now call `net_if_mcast_monitor()`. How should these functions be tweaked?

https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/8dcfa913d0f2d0675b4427bbc7d14302a9f13903/subsys/net/ip/igmp.c#L264-L275
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/8dcfa913d0f2d0675b4427bbc7d14302a9f13903/subsys/net/ip/igmp.c#L294-L304

You would need to remove the code you added to `net_if_ipv4_maddr_add/rm` and just have something like this
```
diff --git a/subsys/net/ip/igmp.c b/subsys/net/ip/igmp.c
index a36444acab..0398f324ae 100644
--- a/subsys/net/ip/igmp.c
+++ b/subsys/net/ip/igmp.c
@@ -285,6 +285,8 @@ int net_ipv4_igmp_join(struct net_if *iface, const struct in_addr *addr)
 
        net_if_ipv4_maddr_join(maddr);
 
+       net_if_mcast_monitor(iface, addr, true);
+
        net_mgmt_event_notify_with_info(NET_EVENT_IPV4_MCAST_JOIN, iface,
                                        &maddr->address.in_addr,
                                        sizeof(struct in_addr));
@@ -312,6 +314,8 @@ int net_ipv4_igmp_leave(struct net_if *iface, const struct in_addr *addr)
 
        net_if_ipv4_maddr_leave(maddr);
 
+       net_if_mcast_monitor(iface, addr, false);
+
        net_mgmt_event_notify_with_info(NET_EVENT_IPV4_MCAST_LEAVE, iface,
                                        &maddr->address.in_addr,
                                        sizeof(struct in_addr));
```

Got it, but with these changes my patch would implement something different than I had in mind. My intention was to allow Ethernet drivers to fit their multicast filters to the actual requirements (dynamically and at runtime). At the moment, they are either using Kconfig like eth_mcux.c...

https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/417647f05715cc183df43ffd841e895c03a486ad/drivers/ethernet/eth_mcux.c#L915-L918
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/417647f05715cc183df43ffd841e895c03a486ad/drivers/ethernet/eth_mcux.c#L973-L975

... or - even worse - disable the multicast filter completely like eth_stm32_hal.c (cf. ad8f837):

https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/417647f05715cc183df43ffd841e895c03a486ad/drivers/ethernet/eth_stm32_hal.c#L135-L147

Staying at mDNS as an example, removing my code from `net_if_ipv4_maddr_add()` would make it impossible for the Ethernet driver to use the mcast monitor to adjust its multicast address filter as the mDNS module is calling `net_if_ipv4_maddr_add()` (in case of IPv4 and `net_ipv6_mld_join()` in case of IPv6 - thus my first approach):

https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/417647f05715cc183df43ffd841e895c03a486ad/subsys/net/lib/dns/mdns_responder.c#L537-L547

As a STM32 and Ethernet stack user struggling with the heavy load that the disabled multicast filters bring, I might better follow the design of the eth_mcux.c driver...

For the multicast to work properly in all cases, the application needs to join the multicast group, it is not enough just to add the multicast address to the network interface. For mDNS, this probably does not matter too much but it does not harm to join the group in that case too. So it might be needed for the mDNS library to join the group instead of just adding the multicast address to the interface. This would require some code changes in mDNS to make it work properly.

> You would need to remove the code you added to `net_if_ipv4_maddr_add/rm` and just have something like this [...]

Followed your advice. Thanks.

> So it might be needed for the mDNS library to join the group instead of just adding the multicast address to the interface. This would require some code changes in mDNS to make it work properly.

I changed that in an additional commit.
